item.description: Frontier Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in robot control, suggesting that broad pretraining provides knowledge valuable for physical action. We ask whether frontier-scale representations can provide a stronger foundation for robot learning. item.description: Visual agents answer questions about ultra-high-resolution photos by zooming into the relevant regions. However, existing agents often answer from common sense instead of reading the evidence. Reinforcement learning (RL) on the final answer cannot correct this, because a guess earns the same reward as reading. item.title: Latent Lattice Language Models
item.description: Language models typically increase per-token computation through deeper or looped layers and latent reasoning steps, while richer residual connections improve information flow across layers. We instead increase computational capacity: the number of active computational states a model maintains. We introduce the Lattice of Latents, a set of per-layer horizontal latent streams that run recurrently along time, alongside the vertical residual stream that flows through depth. item.title: How VLMs Plan What's Next
item.description: When a vision-language model describes an image, it names one object at a time and it rarely repeats itself, yet how the model plans this order is far from obvious. item.title: Optimal Autoregressive Chain-of-Thought Learning via Bagging
item.description: We study how to learn an autoregressive next-token generator $f\colonΣ^\star\toΣ$ from a class $\mathcal{F}$, given chain-of-thought (CoT) demonstrations of length $T$ generated by $f$. item.description: Visual artifact tasks test agents' ability to translate task specifications and source materials into outputs that meet practical needs. Evaluation across artifact families helps distinguish broadly applicable authoring capabilities from strengths confined to a particular medium. item.title: SADL: On the Demand-Supply Geometry of Representation Collapse
item.description: In Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs), a well-constrained projector output does not by itself prevent representation collapse. We find that, from initialization, the encoder representation is dominated by a component shared by different inputs. A batch-normalized projector removes this component, so regularization after the projector cannot correct it, and the differences between representations shrink until they collapse. item.title: Leverage-Enhanced Sampling Owen Method for Explainable Artificial Intelligence
item.description: Recently, the Shapley value has been widely applied in machine learning for feature importance analysis and model explainability. The multilinear extension of games proposed by Owen (1972) expresses the Shapley value as the integral of partial derivatives along the main diagonal of the cube. Direct evaluation of this integral requires exponential-time computation of the partial derivatives. item.title: CertiSum: Bitwise-Identical MXFP4 Training Across Platforms and Parallelism Layouts
item.description: Training with MXFP4, a 4-bit microscaling format, is non-deterministic: identical inputs can produce different results across parallelism layouts and GPU vendors. These differences complicate debugging and training audits and can cause training and inference engines to disagree. We present CertiSum to make MXFP4 training bitwise invariant across runs, parallelism layouts, and GPU vendors. item.title: When Tool Names Are Not Identities: Measuring Provider Misbinding in MCP-Based AI Agents
item.description: Large language model (LLM) applications increasingly act as agents that select and invoke external tools. However, tool metadata used for discovery and selection is not, by itself, necessarily bound to a verified provider identity. This paper studies this gap as tool-provider misbinding: a failure in which a request intended for a legitimate provider is instead resolved to an attacker-controlled tool. item.description: Long video generation should keep the subject and background consistent while supporting rich, natural motion. However, autoregressive models are often distilled with distribution matching distillation (DMD) over short windows, which does not train them to keep this consistency over long ranges. item.title: When Do Histology Foundation Models Need Geometric Test-Time Augmentation?
item.description: Test-time augmentation (TTA) aggregates model predictions across multiple transformed views of an input during inference. However, the rise of self-supervised histology foundation models (FMs) with inherent rotational invariance calls its continued utility into question. item.description: Structure-level wildfire vulnerability assessment is critical for reducing losses in wildland-urban interface communities, yet existing methods often fail to combine parcel-scale ignition pathways with community-scale geographic coverage. This study introduces Wildfire-SSR (Satellite and Street-view for wildfire Risk), a geolocation-aware multimodal framework that integrates macro-scale satellite context with micro-scale street-view evidence. item.title: Reading or Remembering? Measuring Temporal Contamination in Language Models
item.description: Language models are now used to read central-bank text for economic forecasting, but most were trained on text written after the documents they read. item.title: BLIP-Live: Balancing Timeliness & Firing Precision in Proactive Streaming Video Agents
item.description: Streaming video understanding is becoming increasingly important for real-world interactive systems. Such systems must be proactive for natural and useful human interaction: they should respond as soon as sufficient evidence becomes available while avoiding premature, redundant, or incorrect responses. item.title: Benchmarking memory and nonlinear processing capacity of quantum recurrent neural networks for time series prediction
item.description: Quantum machine learning has emerged as a promising approach to time series prediction. While quantum reservoir computing has been widely explored for this setting, variational quantum models tailored to sequential data remain comparatively understudied, largely because they are difficult to train. item.title: ONAM: Fitting Orthogonal Neural Additive Models for Post-Hoc Interpretability of Black-Box Predictions
item.description: Modern machine learning models, such as artificial neural networks, achieve high predictive performance through increasingly complex black-box architectures, limiting their use in settings where transparency, interpretability, and fairness are required. item.title: Seen but Unsaid: Locating and Repairing Cross-Image Comparison in Vision-Language Models
item.description: Vision-language models (VLMs) often fail to match a point or an object across two images, even when the answer can be decoded from their own hidden states. item.title: PLECTA: Overlap-aware instance segmentation of dense strand networks from binary masks
item.description: Many materials and tissues, including carbon-nanotube sheets, collagen and paper, comprise overlapping strands whose arrangement influences their effective properties. item.title: Evaluating Cultural Reasoning and Robustness in LLMs for Spanish Political Discourse
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to interpret, generate, and mediate public-facing language, which makes their reliability especially consequential in politically sensitive settings.
